entries.title: Resource detail title markup corrupted the desktop page layout
entries.expected: The title should remain in the document head and the resource heading, tag list, preview and inspector should render as separate layout regions.
entries.actual: Astro split the interpolated title at the slug expression, placing the closing title/head tags before the trailing text. The browser then parsed resource-header children incorrectly and reduced the preview to 237px at 1280px.
reproduction: Open /resources/ai-prompt-hero/ at 1280x900.
Inspect the document title and resource preview; the title was truncated, the detail DOM was misnested and the preview was too narrow.
entries.rootCause: The Astro template split one title string across multiple text/interpolation segments containing parentheses. The compiler hoisted closing head markup between those segments, corrupting all following body markup.
entries.remediation: Render each resource document title as one Astro expression; align both resource-detail routes on the same semantic header and min-width-safe responsive grid.

entries.title: AI Prompt Composer Execute control was a dead button

entries.title: Unknown resource preview rendered an unrelated Button

entries.title: Workbench dropped nested manifest children when a resource also supplied prop children
entries.expected: The renderer should preserve both explicit resource children and nested ProjectNode children in the rendered slot.
entries.actual: The resource-provided child rendered, but the nested manifest child disappeared from the canvas.

After the fix, both child sources appear in the canvas and in Workbench Preview.
entries.rootCause: NodeRenderer used a nullish fallback from props.children to renderedChildren, making the two valid child sources mutually exclusive.
entries.remediation: Compose explicit and nested children in a single React fragment while honoring the Gold resource's declared children prop contract. A renderer regression and Workbench browser regression cover the user-visible case.

entries.title: Standalone export discarded resource prop children when nested manifest children existed

entries.rootCause: The source generator emitted node.children or props.children as alternatives instead of composing both sources.
entries.remediation: Emit serialized resource prop children followed by generated nested child JSX. The standalone fidelity regression performs a clean package install, build, real browser render, verifies both sources and captures the result.

entries.title: Unsupported resource variants silently fell through to component defaults
entries.expected: A variant outside the resource manifest's declared variant IDs should be rejected with a visible diagnostic and preserved source data.
entries.actual: The deployed Workbench showed the unsupported-variant diagnostic and did not render the invalid Button. Its visible Export action nevertheless downloaded a ZIP; a clean external install passed, but TypeScript failed because the invalid variant was emitted into Overview.tsx.
reproduction: Open a Workbench manifest whose Button node has variant=unsupported-variant.
Open a schema-valid diagnostic manifest with a Button node variant set to unsupported-variant.
On Site v14, verify Workbench shows the unsupported-variant alert and does not render the Button.
Use Workbench Export > Download Standalone React Project; Site v14 downloads a ZIP instead of rejecting it.
Extract outside the repository, install from the exported package.json, and run npm run build; TypeScript reports TS2322 in Overview.tsx.
Locally, generate the same invalid project for Vite and Next; both exporters now throw an error listing quiet, expressive, and nocturne.
entries.rootCause: The generic resource resolver validated declared variants, but the built-in baseline Button resolver in source-tree.ts omitted acceptedVariants in both Vite and Next export maps. That path bypassed the shared validation guard, so Workbench could show an error while the export still emitted invalid Button JSX.
entries.remediation: Keep canonical variant-ID maps for renderer resources and declare the Button's acceptedVariants on both baseline exporter resolver maps. Reject unsupported variants with an actionable error before generating either Vite or Next source. Unit tests reproduce the visible-export defect and pass after the fix; deployed verification remains pending.

deployedVerification.result: FAIL: Workbench displayed an accessible diagnostic and did not render the invalid Button, but the visible Export action downloaded a ZIP instead of rejecting it. A clean external install succeeded; TypeScript failed with TS2322 because the invalid variant was emitted into Overview.tsx.

latestDeployedVerification.result: PASS: deployed Workbench preserved the unsupported variant diagnostic, rejected standalone ZIP export with the supported variant list, and produced no download.

entries.title: Workbench dropped declared resource slot content when nested manifest children existed
entries.expected: A declared resource children slot and nested ProjectNode children should both be represented in the rendered resource when the resource contract permits children.
entries.actual: Workbench showed the nested manifest node but omitted the content supplied through the resource's declared children slot.
reproduction: Load a Workbench project whose canvas-workspace-shell has slots.children set to 'Content from declared resource slot' and a nested child node with 'Content from nested manifest node'.
Before the fix, only the nested node text appeared in the canvas and Preview modal.
After the fix, both the declared slot text and nested node text appear in the canvas and Preview modal.
entries.rootCause: NodeRenderer read explicit child content only from node.props.children and did not use node.slots.children even when the canonical resource prop contract declared the children slot.
entries.remediation: Resolve explicit children from props.children first and then the declared slots.children value, enforce the Gold resource children contract, and compose explicit content with rendered nested nodes. Unit and real Workbench canvas/Preview tests cover both sources.

deployedVerification.result: PASS: deployed Workbench visibly rendered declared slot content and nested manifest children together.

entries.title: Standalone export ignored Workbench responsive node strategies
entries.expected: An exported project should apply the same node-level mobile omit, stack, and collapse strategies as Workbench at the corresponding mobile width.
entries.actual: At 390 px, the exported app still displayed a node marked omit-nonessential and did not apply stack or collapse layout behavior.
reproduction: Export the shared renderer parity fixture as a standalone React/Vite project.
Install dependencies in a clean temporary directory, build, start Vite preview, and open the result at 390x844.
Before the fix, 'Content omitted on mobile' remained visible; the stack and collapse wrappers also lacked their Workbench mobile presentation.
After the fix, the omit node is hidden, the stack wrapper uses a column layout, and the collapse wrapper clips to its defined height.
entries.rootCause: The exporter serialized nodes without responsive strategy metadata, and shared renderer layout CSS had no mobile rules for those strategies.
entries.remediation: Serialize supported responsive strategies on generated node wrappers and add shared mobile container-query rules for omit, stack, and collapse. The same shared fixture now verifies Workbench output and a clean standalone install/build/browser run.

deployedVerification.result: PASS: Workbench 390 preset and the clean exported app at 390px hid the omit node, stacked the stack node, and collapsed the collapse node.

entries.title: Standalone export dropped standard data and accessibility attributes
entries.expected: Generated resource elements should preserve standard data-* and aria-* props as Workbench does, while filtering unsupported ordinary props.
entries.actual: The exported Button omitted data-tracking-id from its resource props, so browser integrations and selectors could not find the element; Workbench retained it.
reproduction: Export the shared renderer parity fixture as a standalone React/Vite project.
Install dependencies in a clean temporary directory, build, start Vite preview, and inspect the desktop page.
Before the fix, query [data-tracking-id="parity-action"]; the locator count was zero and the clean-export browser regression failed.
After the fix, the same locator is visible and the generated app has no console errors or failed requests.

entries.expected: A shopper should be able to open the generated Product Detail screen from the Product Catalog in each direction.
entries.actual: The composed project included a Product Detail screen, but its Product Catalog rendered no link to reach it. Digital music catalogs could also target themselves.
reproduction: Open /compose, enter the ECOM-01 clothing-store brief from the reviewed composition benchmark, and compose.
Inspect Direction 01 and select Product Catalog; the initial preview has no Product Detail action.
Repeat for directions 02 and 03; each catalog lacks the discovery-to-detail link.
entries.rootCause: Product Catalog did not require the conversion-cta role, and the music-store target override matched Product Catalog itself instead of Product Detail.
entries.remediation: Require a conversion action on ecommerce Product Catalog screens, bind it to Product Detail with domain-specific product or album wording, and verify the UI navigation at desktop and mobile widths.

entries.title: Dark product canvases made light resource variants unreadable
entries.expected: Resource variants must retain readable text when composed inside a dark Design DNA canvas, with at least WCAG AA contrast for normal text.
entries.actual: The public v25 Site still had WCAG AA text-contrast failures in 17 of 40 Gold resource previews at both 1440x900 and 390x844 when Expressive resources were shown on the dark canvas. The deployed browser recorded zero console errors, page exceptions, failed requests, and HTTP errors during the scan.
reproduction: Open /compose and enter benchmark brief AI-03.
Compose and open Direction 02, Neural Flow.
Inspect the Support Assistant preview; muted labels on its light timeline panel are nearly unreadable against the dark canvas.
Run the resource contrast regression against all 40 Gold resources with variant=expressive and theme=dark.
entries.rootCause: The site dark utility variant explicitly excluded descendants of .tess-screen, so intended dark styles did not apply within resource previews even though the preview canvas was dark. After enabling those styles, a full Gold scan also exposed resource-specific foreground/background mismatches in dark utility surfaces. Several components used theme-dark text against a fixed light surface, or inherited dark text onto a dark badge/canvas.
entries.remediation: Keep the global .dark utility active inside .tess-screen and preserve that theme boundary in exported resources. Make each affected component declare readable foregrounds for its actual dark or light surface, including local overrides for light surfaces in a dark page. The Playwright regression checks rendered text/background contrast across all 40 Gold resources in Expressive dark mode at desktop and mobile, and the parallel Axe sweep checks WCAG A/AA rules.

regression.before: Public v25 real-browser scan: 17 of 40 Gold Expressive previews failed measured text contrast on desktop and 17 of 40 on mobile. The deployed scan recorded no console errors, uncaught exceptions, failed requests, or HTTP errors.
regression.after: Local production build passed. The all-40 Playwright text/background contrast regression reports 0 findings at 1440x900 and 390x844. The all-40 Gold Axe test reports 0 WCAG A/AA violations at both viewports. Screenshots for all 24 affected resource slugs are captured per viewport.

entries.evidence: Deployed v26 recheck: all 40 Gold resources passed Expressive dark-theme text-contrast checks at 1440x900 and 390x844 with zero findings, console errors, warnings, uncaught errors, failed requests, or HTTP errors. Reports: audit/evidence/v26/gold-dark-contrast-accurate/desktop-chrome/report.json and mobile-chrome/report.json.
entries.verification: Closed after the deployed v26 visible-control scan passed all 40 Gold resources at desktop and mobile with zero contrast findings and clean browser/network diagnostics.

entries.title: Scrollable Gold resource panels were not keyboard reachable
entries.expected: Scrollable resource content must be reachable by keyboard with visible focus, and the mobile Gold-resource Axe sweep must have no serious violations.
entries.actual: The CI mobile Axe run reported scrollable-region-focusable violations in error-state, feature-matrix, and three-pane-app-shell. A local mobile reproduction found the feature-matrix and three-pane-app-shell violations.
reproduction: Run pnpm exec playwright test tests/e2e/resource-dark-expressive-contrast.spec.ts --project=mobile-chrome --workers=1.
Before the fix, Axe reports serious scrollable-region-focusable violations for the affected Gold resources.
Tab through the overflowing code sample, comparison table, and workspace canvas; before the fix these regions are skipped.
entries.rootCause: The resource source contained overflow-auto regions without tabindex, accessible names, or visible focus styling, so keyboard users could not reach their scroll controls.
entries.remediation: Make the scroll regions keyboard focusable, give the table and workspace regions accessible names, provide a visible focus outline, and run the all-Gold mobile Axe sweep plus explicit focus regressions.

regression.before: The CI mobile run found three serious violations; the local mobile run found two.
regression.after: The 40-Gold-resource Axe sweep passes on desktop and mobile; six keyboard and responsive browser checks pass.

entries.title: Three-pane app shell clipped its navigation and inspector on mobile
entries.expected: The resource's collapse strategy should keep navigation, workspace canvas, and inspector visible and usable at its declared 360px mobile width.
entries.actual: The fixed 224px and 256px side panes sat beside the canvas inside a 390px hidden-overflow row, clipping part or all of the inspector.
reproduction: Open /preview/?resource=three-pane-app-shell&variant=expressive&theme=dark at 390x844.
Before the fix, the three fixed-width panes remain in one row and the hidden-overflow shell clips the right pane.
Compare with the after screenshot: navigation, workspace canvas, and inspector are stacked vertically, with no horizontal overflow.
entries.rootCause: The implementation kept a desktop-only fixed-width row despite declaring a responsive collapse strategy and phone-width certification.
entries.remediation: Stack panes on small screens, constrain the canvas width, preserve its scroll access, and restore the three-column workspace at the tablet breakpoint.

regression.before: The CSS fixed the side panes at 14rem and 16rem with overflow hidden on the parent row.
regression.after: The mobile layout test confirms all three panes fit within 390px; desktop retains all three columns without overflow.

entries.title: Whitespace-only brief was accepted and generated directions
entries.expected: A brief containing only whitespace should be rejected, explained beside the field, and never produce a Product Architecture or direction cards.
entries.actual: Submitting spaces and line breaks passed the browser required constraint and composed directions from an empty description.
reproduction: Open /compose and wait for Catalogue ready.
Enter spaces and line breaks only, then select Compose Interface System.
Before the fix, no alert appeared and generated direction cards remained visible.
entries.rootCause: The submit handler did not trim or validate the description before calling the deterministic composition pipeline; HTML required validation considers whitespace non-empty.
entries.remediation: Trim the description before composition. Reject empty normalized input, focus the field, and expose an associated alert with aria-invalid.

regression.before: Visible UI browser checks failed on desktop and mobile: no validation alert was shown and directions could be generated from whitespace.
regression.after: Both browser projects reject the input, focus the field, expose an accessible error, and show no direction cards.

entries.title: Edited Compose inputs left directions for the previous brief available
entries.expected: Any change to the brief or design controls should make prior generated directions unavailable until the user composes again.
entries.actual: Old Product Architecture and direction cards remained available after editing the brief or Visual Ambition, so the user could open a project that did not match the current form.
reproduction: Compose a product brief and wait for all three direction cards.
Edit the brief or change Visual Ambition.
Before the fix, the original directions remained visible and actionable.
entries.rootCause: The output was gated only by a hasComposed flag and catalogue readiness; the rendered controls were not compared with the input snapshot used for composition.
entries.remediation: Fingerprint the normalized brief and all composition controls at submit. Hide stale output and announce that the user must compose again when the fingerprint changes.

regression.before: Separate visible UI browser tests failed on the old source: both editing the brief and changing Visual Ambition left the previous direction cards available; the setting-specific run produced no stale-state status.
regression.after: The 16-run desktop/mobile suite hides stale directions after either a brief or setting change and announces that recomposition is required.

entries.title: Compose toggle choices did not expose their selected state
entries.expected: Visual Ambition, Structural Creativity, and target-device choices should expose their current selection to keyboard and assistive-technology users.
entries.actual: Selected buttons changed color but had no pressed state or named toggle group.
reproduction: Open /compose and focus a Visual Ambition or Structural Creativity stop.
Use Enter or Space to select a different stop.
Before the fix, the visual style changed but aria-pressed was absent.
entries.rootCause: The controls were ordinary buttons with color-only selected styling and no grouped or pressed semantics.
entries.remediation: Add accessible labels to toggle groups and expose each selected state through aria-pressed while preserving existing keyboard button interaction.

regression.before: Desktop and mobile checks found selected controls without aria-pressed.
regression.after: Enter and Space operate the toggles, the selected state is announced, and the 390px Compose document has no horizontal overflow.

entries.title: Last selected target device looked active but silently refused removal
entries.expected: A user should understand that at least one target device must remain selected and the final selected control should not look actionable.
entries.actual: The final selected device button remained enabled and visually active; clicking it caused no state change and gave no explanation.
reproduction: Open Advanced Constraints & Devices.
Remove devices until one remains.
Click the remaining selected device; before the fix, it remained selected without feedback.
entries.rootCause: The toggle handler prevented an empty target list, but the view did not reflect that invariant or explain the refused interaction.
entries.remediation: Disable the final selected device button, expose pressed state for all device toggles, and announce the minimum-one-device rule.

regression.before: The last selected device remained enabled and no explanation appeared.
regression.after: The last selected device is disabled and a status message explains the constraint on both desktop and mobile.

entries.title: Selecting a valid sample brief left the previous input error visible
entries.expected: Loading a valid sample brief should clear the empty-brief alert and invalid field state.
entries.actual: After an empty submission, selecting the Playful HR Platform sample updated the brief but left the prior error visible.
reproduction: Open /compose and submit a whitespace-only brief.
Select the Playful HR Platform sample brief.
Before the fix, the validation alert and aria-invalid state persisted beside a valid description.
entries.rootCause: The manual text-input handler cleared the validation error, but the separate sample-brief selection handler updated form state without clearing validation state.
entries.remediation: Clear the validation error when a valid sample brief is selected and verify the alert and invalid state disappear.

regression.before: The visible regression failed: one alert remained after the valid sample was selected.
regression.after: The test passes on desktop and mobile; the alert is removed and aria-invalid is cleared.

entries.title: Canvas taps on disabled resource actions did not select the resource
entries.expected: Tapping a disabled resource action in the canvas should select its containing node and open Inspect without activating the disabled action.
entries.actual: The disabled Explore Interface System button swallowed the pointer interaction, leaving the mobile Workbench on Preview with no selected node.
reproduction: Compose the employee-experience brief, open Direction C in Workbench, and switch to Settings & Policies.
Tap the disabled Explore Interface System button in the canvas.
Before the fix, Preview remained active and the inspector showed no selected node.
entries.rootCause: Native disabled controls suppress the click event used by the Workbench canvas selection handler, so the containing resource node never received selection.
entries.remediation: Capture pointerdown on the containing resource node when its target is disabled, prevent the disabled action, and select the node. Keep the action disabled until it has a connected behavior.

regression.before: The visible mobile regression failed at the inspector assertion when the disabled resource action was tapped.
regression.after: The visible mobile regression passes; the same tap selects the containing component, opens Inspect, and the action remains disabled.

entries.title: Composition flattened resource kinds into section nodes
entries.expected: Composed resource nodes should preserve the catalogue kind in ProjectManifest.nodeType so the Workbench exposes layout, section, block, component, and element hierarchy accurately.
entries.actual: The composition pipeline assigned section to every non-navigation resource, so block, component, and primitive resources appeared as sections and the generated tree contained no truthful component or element levels.
reproduction: Compose the exact employee-experience brief through /compose and open Direction C in Workbench.
Inspect the visible Layers tree and select resource-backed nodes.
Before the fix, an entity-profile-header block was serialized with nodeType section; the type contract regression failed.
entries.rootCause: composeProjectForDirection hard-coded section for every resource-backed node except navigation, discarding ResourceManifest.resourceType.
entries.remediation: Derive the editor node type from the selected catalogue resource type, with navigation retained as layout, then verify the visible tree and inspector expose root, section, component, and element selection.

regression.before: The new composer contract test failed because a block resource was emitted as section.
regression.after: The composer contract and desktop/mobile visible selection journeys pass with resource-kind-preserving nodes.

entries.title: Project DNA values were labelled inherited
entries.expected: When no node is selected, Design DNA status labels should identify the project as the value source. Node scopes should continue to distinguish inherited, overridden, and locked values.
entries.actual: The Feel Mixer, Visual Ambition, and Structural Creativity all displayed INHERITED while Project Scope was active, even though those values were the project-level source.
reproduction: Compose the exact employee-experience brief, open Direction C, and open the Workbench at 1440×900.
Select any node, then use Deselect Node to enter Project Scope.
Inspect the Feel Mixer, Visual Ambition, and Structural Creativity status badges. Before the fix all seven badges read INHERITED.
entries.rootCause: FeelMixer and IntentTab treated a missing selected node as the inherited state instead of as the project-level source scope.
entries.remediation: Render Project at project scope, Inherited or Overridden at an editable node scope, and Locked where a local or ancestor lock applies. A browser regression checks all seven project-scope labels and representative mobile inheritance.

regression.before: The visible desktop assertion failed because the Project label was absent and the seven values were reported as inherited.
regression.after: Desktop shows seven Project labels at Project Scope; mobile shows the Project source and inherited child value. Both runs report zero console errors, warnings, uncaught exceptions, failed requests, and HTTP errors.

entries.title: DNA lock snapshot behavior was not explained after unlocking
entries.expected: The lock control should explain that a lock preserves current effective DNA as local values and that Reset to Inherited resumes ancestor values after unlocking.
entries.actual: Lock Design DNA only said it protected overrides during global recomposition. After unlock, inherited values appeared as local overrides and required an explicit reset without explaining why.
reproduction: In Workbench, select a node inheriting from its parent and lock Design DNA.
Change the parent value while the child remains locked, then unlock the child.
Observe that the child retains its frozen value as an override and that Reset to Inherited restores the new parent value.
entries.rootCause: The lock description documented protection during recomposition but omitted that the frozen effective values remain local after unlock until explicitly reset.
entries.remediation: Explain the snapshot and reset behavior in the Lock Design DNA control and name the ancestor inheritance behavior in the reset tooltip. The visible browser regression verifies locked, overridden-after-unlock, and inherited-after-reset states.

regression.before: The visible test expected immediate inheritance after unlock and received the frozen snapshot; the saved screenshot showed six DNA properties marked Overridden and a Reset to Inherited control with no explanation.
regression.after: The Locks panel explains snapshot persistence. The desktop regression confirms the frozen child value remains local after unlock, then Reset to Inherited picks up the changed parent value with no runtime or network errors.

entries.title: Duplicating a screen could produce an invalid project route
entries.expected: Every duplicate screen should receive a unique route and fresh screen/node identities so the manifest remains valid.
entries.actual: Two rapid duplicates of the root route both appeared as Marketing Home (Copy) at /-copy. The visible UI accepted both and the downloaded manifest failed canonical validation for duplicate routes.
reproduction: Open the Playful HR showcase in Workbench at 1440x900.
Open Pages and duplicate Marketing Home twice.
Inspect the two copy rows and export the manifest.
entries.rootCause: The duplicate handler always appended a fixed -copy suffix and copy name without checking existing screens. For root route /, both copies therefore became /-copy. Screen IDs were also derived from millisecond timestamps, which risked collisions under rapid duplication.
entries.remediation: Normalize the source route with the screen name as the root fallback, allocate a unique copy suffix from the current screens, use createId for screen identities, and verify the downloaded manifest against ProjectManifestSchema.

regression.before: The visible regression failed: both copies had route /-copy, and canonical manifest validation returned false.
regression.after: Two copies receive /marketing-home-copy and /marketing-home-copy-2; screen/node IDs and routes are unique, and the exported manifest validates.

entries.title: Add Page accepted a route already assigned to another screen
entries.expected: The Add Page form should reject a normalized route collision, show an accessible error, and leave the screen list unchanged.
entries.actual: Submitting /people created an eighth screen even though /people already belonged to People Directory; no alert explained the collision.
reproduction: Open the Playful HR showcase in Workbench at 1440x900.
Open Pages, choose Add Page, enter a new title and /people as the route.
Submit and observe that the duplicate route is added without an error.
entries.rootCause: The Add Page handler normalized slashes and case for display but did not compare the candidate route with routes already in the manifest before calling addScreen.
entries.remediation: Normalize both existing and proposed routes, reject a duplicate before mutation, and render a role=alert message. The regression checks that the count remains 7 for /people and that a unique route can then be added.

regression.before: The baseline browser run showed screen count 7 before submit and 8 after; the expected alert was absent.
regression.after: The browser run shows count 7 before and after /people, exposes an accessible collision message, then accepts /people-route-check.

entries.title: Tree mutation engine actions were not reachable from the Layers UI
entries.expected: A selected non-root layer should expose usable duplicate, sibling move, and confirmed delete actions; invalid root and locked operations should be disabled with an explanation.
entries.actual: The Layers panel exposed selection, expansion, and lock toggles, but no Duplicate, Move, or Delete controls. Playwright could not find the expected root-disabled Duplicate action.
reproduction: Open the Playful HR showcase in Workbench at 1440x900.
Select Layers and select the screen root.
Observe the missing selected-layer action group; repeat with a non-root layer.
entries.rootCause: The mutation executor supported INSERT_NODE, MOVE_NODE and DELETE_NODE, but LayersTab rendered only lock toggles and did not connect those operations to user controls.
entries.remediation: Expose actions for selected non-root nodes through the existing mutation/history path; preserve root/ancestor-lock guards, require a second delete action, provide keyboard selection and visible status, and document that Move is sibling-only.

regression.before: The baseline browser run failed because the selected root had no Duplicate action or disabled-state explanation.
regression.after: Desktop and 390x844 browser checks verify root/lock guard messages, keyboard selection, duplicate/move/delete, exact undo/redo, schema-valid export, and action reachability above the mobile navigation.

entries.title: Workbench mutation capabilities were inaccurately classified
entries.expected: Each advertised mutation verb should have distinct observable semantics, or be labelled experimental and excluded from Core workflows.
entries.actual: Improve, Simplify, Intensify, and Match DNA appeared as Beta rows despite lacking separate deterministic operation contracts; no corresponding mutation controls existed in the Workbench. The visible selected-layer actions exposed only concrete duplicate, sibling move, delete, lock and unlock controls.
reproduction: Review the Step 19 mutation inventory and Workbench mutation specification.
Compare the listed Improve, Simplify, Intensify and Match DNA operations with the visible Workbench controls and mutation schema.
Observe that no operation-specific behavior or acceptance criteria are defined.
entries.rootCause: Natural-language intent labels were recorded as shipped mutation features without an operation-specific target, output contract, or observable result.
entries.remediation: Classify these verbs as Lab until their behavior and safety criteria are defined, keep unsupported natural-language proposals out of production mutation controls, and record Hide as Lab because ProjectNode has no persisted visibility field.

regression.before: The inventory and Workbench contract described unsupported verbs as Beta or as available layer actions.
regression.after: The inventory and matrix mark the unspecified verbs Lab, and the Workbench contract lists only implemented controls and their limits.

entries.title: Mobile Workbench hid structural-action results outside the Command tab
entries.expected: After Recompose or Surprise Me, the Workbench should announce the completed action and its outcome on the current mobile tab.
entries.actual: The manifest changed and locked content remained intact, but the success explanation was rendered only inside CommandBar, which is not mounted while Pages or other mobile tabs are active.
reproduction: At 390x844, open the Playful HR showcase in Workbench and select Pages.
Lock the Team Overview KPI subtree, then click Recompose.
Export the manifest and confirm the workspace hierarchy changed while the locked KPI subtree remained identical; observe that no role=status feedback is visible.
Repeat with Surprise Me and observe that the manifest changes but the explanation is absent from the active tab.
entries.rootCause: MobileWorkbench mounted CommandBar only on the Command tab, while the store's lastActionMessage was consumed only by CommandBar. Other active tabs therefore hid feedback for successful top-toolbar mutations.
entries.remediation: Subscribe to the shared lastActionMessage in MobileWorkbench and render it as a polite status region below the toolbar on non-Command tabs. Keep the detailed message in CommandBar when that tab is active. Add desktop/mobile browser regressions for both structural actions and ensure the live status fits the viewport.

regression.before: Both mobile browser tests observed mutationApplied=true and feedbackVisible=false, then failed because no role=status element existed on the active Pages tab.
regression.after: Desktop and 390x844 browser tests confirm the status region announces Recompose and Surprise Me, remains within viewport bounds, and the resulting manifests preserve locked subtrees, resolve all catalogue resources, and undo/redo exactly.

entries.title: Undo and redo history disappeared after reloading a local project
entries.expected: After a project edit is saved locally, refreshing Workbench should preserve the bounded undo and redo stacks so the user can restore exact recent states.
entries.actual: The latest manifest remained available after reload, but Workbench reset history and future to empty arrays. Undo was disabled despite 51 visible Design DNA edits immediately before reload.
reproduction: At 1440x900 or 390x844, open the Playful HR showcase in Workbench and open Project Scope > Intent.
Use the Visual Ambition slider to create 51 sequential keyboard edits; export the final manifest and verify the slider reads 51.
Reload the Workbench URL. The manifest remains at 51, but Undo is disabled and none of the prior states can be restored.
entries.rootCause: WorkbenchShell persisted the current ProjectManifest and checkpoint journal, but not the in-memory history and future stacks. setManifest correctly reset those arrays on load, leaving the saved project without its recent edit history.
entries.remediation: Persist bounded, schema-validated history stacks in a versioned IndexedDB store using immutable snapshots and a small stack pointer; coalesce rapid UI edits so the newest state is durable before the save status reports Saved; restore history before enabling the loaded Workbench; cap checkpoint restoration to the same 50-step window; and show local history save state in the toolbar.

regression.before: The baseline desktop and mobile reports record 51 visible edits, a project manifest restored at ambition 51, and undoEnabledAfterReload=false. The browser regression failed on the disabled Undo control.
regression.after: Desktop and mobile browser tests preserve the 50-step history window across reload, undo all 50 edits to the exact retained manifest, redo all 50 to the exact final manifest, and restore a named checkpoint after another reload. Each report records zero console errors or warnings, uncaught exceptions, failed requests, and HTTP errors.

entries.title: Blending a project overwrote the source project history
entries.expected: Creating and reloading a blended project should leave its source project and undo history independently reloadable.
entries.actual: After Blend wrote source snapshots under the new project ID, reopening the source project entered recovery mode because one of its history snapshots had been overwritten.
reproduction: Open a Compose direction in Workbench and record its project URL and manifest.
Change Visual Ambition through the visible Intent control and wait for the local history status to report Saved.
Use Blend to create a new project, reload it, then reopen the source project URL.
The source project displays Local project needs attention with a missing undo history snapshot error.
entries.rootCause: History snapshot IDs were generated per manifest object but the IndexedDB key was global. When Blend reused a source manifest snapshot in the new project history, its record was overwritten with the blended project ownership metadata, so the source pointer referenced a missing record.
entries.remediation: Allocate each snapshot ID within its owning project scope and include that owner in the IndexedDB key. Keep the same manifest object mapped to distinct snapshot IDs when it belongs to multiple project histories.

regression.before: The visible-browser regression passed through Blend and blended-project reload, then failed when returning to the source project. The source UI entered recovery mode with a missing history snapshot. The baseline report records zero console errors, failed requests, or HTTP errors.
regression.after: The same desktop UI regression reloads the blended project, returns to the source project, confirms Undo is enabled, and undoes the source edit to its prior Design DNA value. The report records zero console errors, failed requests, or HTTP errors.

entries.title: A blocked localStorage read prevented IndexedDB project recovery
entries.expected: A stored project should load from IndexedDB when browser policy denies localStorage reads.
entries.actual: Workbench showed a recovery error despite a valid project and undo history in IndexedDB.
reproduction: Open a saved Workbench project at 1440×900 or 390×844.
Deny reads for its project and active-project localStorage keys, then reload.
Before the fix, Workbench stops rather than restoring the IndexedDB project.
entries.rootCause: The browser loader read the synchronous journal without isolating per-key SecurityError exceptions, aborting the independent IndexedDB lookup.
entries.remediation: Catch journal read failures independently, continue with the durable store, and show which store recovered the project.

regression.before: The visible browser regression reproduced the failure at desktop and mobile viewports.
regression.after: The matching browser regression passed at desktop and mobile viewports; runtime reports record zero console errors or warnings, uncaught exceptions, failed requests, or HTTP errors.

entries.title: A full recovery journal treated a successful database save as fatal
entries.expected: A quota failure in the synchronous recovery journal should not block a successful IndexedDB save.
entries.actual: Workbench stopped after localStorage raised QuotaExceededError even though IndexedDB could persist the project.
reproduction: Make localStorage.setItem throw QuotaExceededError.
Open Workbench, edit Visual Ambition, then reload.
Before the fix, the UI blocks before using IndexedDB.
entries.rootCause: The synchronous journal write was reported as a fatal save error before the independent database write completed.
entries.remediation: Catch journal and database failures independently, persist through IndexedDB, and report the available recovery path.

regression.before: The visible browser regression reproduced the failure at desktop and mobile viewports.
regression.after: The matching browser regression passed at desktop and mobile viewports; runtime reports record zero console errors or warnings, uncaught exceptions, failed requests, or HTTP errors.

entries.title: IndexedDB failure blocked journal-backed editing and history recovery
entries.expected: When IndexedDB is unavailable, a valid local recovery journal should keep the project editable with an explicit history limitation.
entries.actual: Project, history, or checkpoint database errors sent Workbench into a fatal recovery screen despite a usable journal.
reproduction: Make IDBFactory.open fail.
Open a showcase as a local project, edit its DNA, and reload.
Before the fix, initial save or history/checkpoint reads end the Workbench.
entries.rootCause: Optional IndexedDB reads and writes for project, history, and checkpoint state shared the fatal load path even when localStorage retained the current project.
entries.remediation: Keep journal-backed editing available, isolate optional history/checkpoint failures, and label history as limited.

regression.before: The visible browser regression reproduced the failure at desktop and mobile viewports.
regression.after: The matching browser regression passed at desktop and mobile viewports; runtime reports record zero console errors or warnings, uncaught exceptions, failed requests, or HTTP errors.

entries.title: Legacy project migrations were not written back to browser storage
entries.expected: A successfully migrated project should be saved in the canonical schema so subsequent reloads use the migrated record.
entries.actual: Workbench rendered the migrated project in memory while browser storage still contained schema 0.1.0.
reproduction: Seed a valid schema 0.1.0 project in the browser journal.
Open its Workbench URL and inspect the stored record.
Before the fix, the UI displays schema 1.0.0 but storage remains at 0.1.0.
entries.rootCause: The loader did not report that migration occurred, so Workbench never persisted the validated canonical manifest.
entries.remediation: Track successful migration and save the current-schema manifest to browser storage when the project opens.

regression.before: The visible browser regression reproduced the failure at desktop and mobile viewports.
regression.after: The matching browser regression passed at desktop and mobile viewports; runtime reports record zero console errors or warnings, uncaught exceptions, failed requests, or HTTP errors.

entries.title: Mirrored corrupt project data appeared twice in recovery mode
entries.expected: A damaged raw record mirrored across the per-project and active-project journals should appear once, while distinct records remain separately recoverable.
entries.actual: Safe recovery displayed duplicate raw-record export links for the same malformed project payload.
reproduction: Store the same malformed raw project in its project-specific and active-project journal keys.
Open the project URL and inspect recovery exports.
Before the fix, the same record appears twice.
entries.rootCause: The loader appended journal entries independently without deduplicating identical raw payload and validation-reason pairs.
entries.remediation: Deduplicate identical damaged records while preserving the raw payload and any distinct corruption records.

regression.before: The visible browser regression reproduced the failure at desktop and mobile viewports.
regression.after: The matching browser regression passed at desktop and mobile viewports; runtime reports record zero console errors or warnings, uncaught exceptions, failed requests, or HTTP errors.

entries.title: Total storage failure falsely claimed a durable save
entries.expected: When both persistent stores fail, Workbench should clearly say the project is unsaved and offer export.
entries.actual: The warning claimed the project had been saved in the recovery journal even though journal writes hit quota and IndexedDB was unavailable.
reproduction: Disable IndexedDB and make all Tessellate localStorage writes throw QuotaExceededError.
Open /workbench and inspect the storage warning.
Before the fix, it falsely promises a durable journal save.
entries.rootCause: The in-memory fallback was reported as journal-backed even after the journal write failed.
entries.remediation: Distinguish memory-only state from a successful journal fallback; warn that data is unsaved and prompt manifest export.

regression.before: The browser regression is configured to save a before capture if the false recovery-journal claim appears; no before capture was produced in this run.
regression.after: Desktop and mobile reports confirm that the unavailable stores are reported truthfully, the current manifest remains exportable, and editing remains available, with no console errors or warnings, uncaught exceptions, failed requests, or HTTP errors.

entries.title: User-authored semantic copy broke standalone React/Vite builds
entries.expected: User text in built-in navigation, KPI, action, and status roles should compile into a standalone project and render literally as text.
entries.actual: The Vite generator inserted authored values directly into quoted JSX attributes and raw JSX children. Quotes and angle-bracket text made the extracted clean project fail TypeScript compilation with TS1003, TS1382, and TS1002.
reproduction: Create a valid ProjectManifest with navigation-header, metric-kpi, action-button, and status-indicator nodes whose user-authored values contain double quotes, apostrophes, <, and &.
Generate the React/Vite ZIP and extract it into a fresh temporary directory outside the Tessellate repository.
Install dependencies from the exported package.json and run pnpm build.
Before the fix, tsc fails while parsing the generated screen component.
entries.rootCause: The semantic-role branches in generateScreenCode emitted raw string values in JSX attributes and text rather than serializing them into JavaScript expressions.

Inspect the Tessellate command input name.

entries.title: Compose blocked its first response frame during generation
entries.expected: Compose should acknowledge the action promptly while preserving all three fully rendered directions.
entries.actual: Before the fix, the Compose pointer interaction measured 299 ms INP. After yielding a visible busy frame, it measured 32 ms; the exact employee brief still generated all three previews.
reproduction: Open /compose at 1440x900 and wait for Catalogue ready.
Enter the exact employee-experience brief, select Refined and Radical, and submit Compose while a Chrome DevTools performance trace is recording.
Inspect the longest interaction and verify all three generated direction previews.
network: 22 route requests: 20 HTTP 200 and 2 HTTP 304; no failed requests.
entries.rootCause: composeProjectPipeline ran in the submit task before React could paint feedback, so the click waited for product interpretation and resource selection.
entries.verification: A Chrome DevTools trace on the local Sites Worker measured the post-fix pointer interaction at 32 ms (0.8 ms input delay, 11 ms processing, 20 ms presentation), LCP 119 ms, and CLS 0.00. The exact brief rendered three directions. Desktop/mobile CPU-throttled E2E confirms the visible busy state and completion. Console errors and warnings were absent. Published review verification remains pending.

entries.title: Metrics resource metadata claimed unmeasured infrastructure outcomes
entries.expected: The resource description and use guidance should match its four illustrative project, team, task, and completion values.

reproduction: Open /r/customer-metrics-strip at desktop or mobile width.
Compare the detail description, summary, ideal/avoid guidance, and job statement with the default preview values.

entries.rootCause: The canonical resource manifest and README were written for generic infrastructure credibility rather than the actual sample data rendered by the component.
entries.verification: Replaced the unsupported outcome claims with project/team/task/completion copy, labeled the defaults illustrative, and added desktop/mobile Sites Worker assertions plus screenshots and machine-readable runtime evidence. After rebuilding the Sites static artifact, both browser cases pass with HTTP 200 and zero console errors, warnings, uncaught exceptions, failed requests, or HTTP errors. Public review verification remains pending.

entries.title: Default marquee wordmarks implied real customer relationships

Before the fix, tests/e2e/resource-copy-truthfulness-step-39.spec.ts failed on desktop and mobile because neither the copy nor preview identified the vendor names as samples.
network: The deployed route returned HTTP 200 at both viewports; there were no failed requests or HTTP errors.
entries.rootCause: The component hardcoded real vendor names as defaults while its metadata described customer and partner proof without approval or sample disclosure.
entries.verification: Replaced vendor names with clearly marked sample partner labels, disclosed the default data in the component and metadata, and retained caller-supplied real names without the sample note. The desktop/mobile Sites Worker regression passes with HTTP 200, zero console warnings/errors, uncaught exceptions, failed requests, or HTTP errors. Public review verification remains pending.

entries.title: Centered marquee overflow clipped its first wordmark
entries.expected: The first wordmark should be visible at the initial scroll position, with remaining names reachable by pointer and keyboard scrolling.

At scrollLeft 0, compare the first wordmark's left edge with the scroll viewport's left edge.

network: The deployed route returned HTTP 200 at both viewports; there were no failed requests or HTTP errors.
entries.rootCause: The same element used overflow-x-auto and justify-center, so a content row wider than its viewport was centered with negative overflow on both sides.
entries.verification: Separated the keyboard-focusable scroll viewport from its max-content flex track. The browser regression verifies the first name begins at the viewport edge, horizontal scrolling remains available, the region receives focus, and ArrowRight changes its scroll position on desktop and mobile. Screenshots and geometry records show firstLeft equals trackLeft (24 CSS pixels); public review verification remains pending.

entries.title: Homepage visual spectrum controls were active before island hydration
entries.expected: Below-fold demo controls should remain disabled with a visible explanation until their client handlers are ready.
entries.actual: The SSR-rendered Essential control appeared enabled while JavaScript was disabled; in the desktop Sites Worker run, clicking it before the client island attached left the demo on Elevated with no feedback. The equivalent mobile run passed.
reproduction: Open / and scroll the Essential → Experimental section into view.
Activate 01 · Essential as soon as it enters view, before client hydration completes.
Observe that the mode remains Elevated; the before screenshot and JSON show the server-rendered button enabled without a preparing status.
network: The local Sites Worker route returned HTTP 200; the before capture reported zero console errors or warnings, uncaught exceptions, failed requests, and HTTP errors.
entries.rootCause: The interactive React island used client:visible but rendered enabled server-side buttons, so users could activate controls before hydration attached event handlers.
entries.verification: Closed after issue-specific verification on the public v30 Site (2026-10-25). At both 1440x900 and 390x844, the fresh route showed the three spectrum controls disabled with the visible Preparing comparison controls status. Scrolling to the section hydrated the island; selecting 03 · Experimental changed aria-pressed to true and displayed Level 03 · Ambition 75–95. No uncaught exception, failed request, or bad HTTP response occurred. Each page still emitted the separate Sites-injected strict-CSP console error recorded as AUD-342. Machine evidence and screenshots: quality/evidence/step-39/deployed-v30-home-spectrum.json and its screenshot paths.

entries.title: Unbounded collections exposed validation to excessive work
entries.expected: External collection sizes should be bounded and all workspace packages should resolve a patched Zod version.
entries.actual: The dependency graph included affected zod@4.6.5 and multiple Zod majors; public collection schemas without maximum sizes could validate arbitrarily large arrays.

Submit 25,000 malformed entries to the project-screen and recursive-child schemas; before bounds, schemas did not reject the collection length before item validation.
entries.rootCause: Core external collection contracts lacked explicit maxima and packages resolved multiple Zod majors, including the affected 4.6.5 release.
entries.verification: The schema suite passes 144 tests including 25,000-entry hostile collection regressions; full typecheck and lint pass; pnpm audit:all passes all 16 behavioral gates, 324/324 resource isolation, 718-page Astro plus Sites build, bundle budgets, provenance, secret/security and dependency audits; the complete Playwright run passes 274 app, 224 Sites Worker and 3 preview tests with 144 configured skips and zero failures. Public release verification remains pending.

entries.title: MCP SDK dependency graph included vulnerable body-parser 2.3.0
entries.expected: The installed dependency graph must resolve body-parser to a release outside the high-severity advisory's affected range.
entries.actual: The workspace resolved body-parser@2.3.0 through express@5.3.0 under @modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.32.1. GHSA-27r3-jxmh-p828 affects body-parser 2.x before 2.4.0; pnpm audit failed the dependency gate. reproduction: Run pnpm audit:all before the fix; the final dependency phase reports GHSA-27r3-jxmh-p828 as high severity.
Run pnpm why body-parser -r; before the fix it reports body-parser@2.3.0 beneath @modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.32.1.
entries.rootCause: The SDK's Express dependency graph selected the latest locked body-parser release 2.3.0 and the workspace had no patched-version override.
entries.verification: The workspace override resolves body-parser@2.4.0; pnpm install --frozen-lockfile passes, pnpm audit reports no known vulnerabilities, the MCP client/SSE workflow tests pass 7/7, and pnpm audit:all passes 16/16 behavioral gates, 324/324 resource-isolation scans, production builds, bundle budgets, license/provenance, secrets/security, and dependency audits. Published release verification remains pending.

entries.title: Documentation index omitted all canonical repository guides
entries.expected: The documentation landing page should link to the repository product, architecture, design, schema, security, deployment, and operating guides it claims to expose.
entries.actual: The page rendered one hard-coded Registry installation link and no canonical Markdown guide links. The 15 Markdown-backed detail routes were not generated.

entries.verification: Changed the glob to the repository-root docs directory. The Astro build generates all 15 canonical Markdown detail routes; the desktop and mobile browser regression passes, verifies 16 links including the Registry installation guide, and opens the Product Specification page. Full local release gates pass; public review verification remains pending.

entries.title: Identical manifests produced timestamp-dependent exports
entries.expected: Repeated exports of the same valid manifest and target should have identical file paths and bytes so Workbench, CLI, MCP and standalone output are reproducible.

entries.title: Missing-project recovery offered an unrelated manifest export

Sites Worker browser regression passes at 1440x900 and 390x844; the state has zero Axe violations, console/page errors, failed requests, HTTP errors, and horizontal overflow. entries.title: Homepage composer default brief describes an unrelated finance product
entries.expected: A clean visitor should see a relevant example brief that represents Tessellate's product and can be composed without first removing unrelated domain content.

Observe six fields without either attribute in Site v20.

entries.title: Mobile header actions exceeded the narrow viewport
entries.expected: The public header should keep its navigation actions visible without widening the document beyond the viewport.
entries.actual: At 320px, the original full-width action label and 12px gaps produced document scrollWidth 336px (viewport clientWidth 320px). The pull-request CI run also measured 376px at a 360px viewport. The new mobile header layout measures 320px at 320px locally.

The header exposes the established Start building accessible name while showing a compact visible label below 400px. The full local browser run passes with 548 passed, 149 configured skips, and zero failures; the Sites Worker certifies all 324 resources. entries.title: Typing a debounced search hid current Explore results and tore down previews
entries.expected: The current result cards and their isolated previews remain visible while a debounced query is being entered; the result set updates after the query is committed.
entries.actual: Before the fix, entering a query immediately switched the result cards to skeletons even though the committed query had not changed. The accessible count changed to 'Searching catalogue...', the previous resource links disappeared, and in-flight preview frames were unmounted.
reproduction: Open /explore/ at desktop or mobile size and wait for 'Showing 50 of 324 resources'.
Scroll the first resource card into view so its sandboxed /preview-content/ iframe starts loading.
Enter 'onboarding' in Search catalogue and inspect the page within the debounce interval.
Before the fix, the prior result disappeared into a skeleton grid before the query was applied.
entries.rootCause: The pending-state comparison used the live input value rather than the debounced committed query. A keystroke therefore marked the previous, still-valid results as stale and replaced their cards, which also removed preview iframes.
entries.verification: The public v20 browser run at 929x861 typed onboarding through the visible search field and observed the prior 50 result links plus the same four preview iframe DOM nodes retained through 273ms; after commit, the view showed 15 onboarding results. The browser regression also holds a preview request in flight and verifies it is not canceled. The constrained 4G/4x CPU release gate classifies expected iframe cancellations by frame origin.

entries.title: An old zero-results state remained visible while a new query was debouncing
entries.expected: When the previous search has zero results and the visitor enters a new query, Explore should replace the stale empty state with an explicit pending-search status until the new result set is ready.
entries.actual: The empty-state heading and 'Showing 0 of 0 resources' remained visible for about 19ms after typing 'onboarding', before 15 results appeared. The input already contained a different query, so the status described stale results as current.
reproduction: Open /explore/ at 500x844 and wait for the catalogue to load.
Search for 'no-resource-should-match-this-query' and wait for the empty state.
Replace it with 'onboarding' and observe the accessible summary during the next 250ms debounce interval.
entries.rootCause: After preserving populated result cards during debounce, the no-results branch considered only a committed search to be pending. It did not account for a new live query while the previous committed query had zero hits.
entries.verification: The Sites Worker regression first failed with the stale zero-results summary, then passed after the empty-result branch began showing the pending-search state during query debounce. It verifies that an explicit searching indicator appears and the old empty state never flashes. Public Site verification remains pending.

entries.title: Zod's caught eval capability probe triggered a strict CSP violation
entries.expected: Explore hydrates and validates catalogue data without any script-src eval violation under the strict application CSP.
entries.actual: Before the fix, Chromium recorded one securitypolicyviolation with effectiveDirective script-src and blockedURI eval from the bundled Zod validator module. Zod caught the blocked Function probe, so the page still loaded. After the fix, desktop and mobile Sites Worker regressions report no eval violation; the 324-resource catalogue and previews load.
reproduction: Build the Sites Worker artifact and open /explore at 1440x900 or 390x844.
Attach a securitypolicyviolation listener before navigation and filter for blockedURI === 'eval'.
Before the fix, the listener received one script-src event from the bundled Zod module even though no console error or failed request occurred.
After the fix, run the public Explore avoids Zod eval probes under the strict application CSP regression in both Sites Chromium profiles.
network: After fix: Explore page, catalogue JSON, scripts, styles, fonts, and requested resource previews returned HTTP 200; no failed requests in the 108-request desktop load.

Public v30 remains unchanged; deployed confirmation is required before this issue can be closed.

entries.title: Product Preview CTA opens Compose inside the isolated iframe
entries.expected: Activating a product-preview link should take the user to the full top-level application route while preserving preview isolation.
entries.actual: On public v30, START COMPOSING left the top-level URL at /r/cta-product-preview and navigated only the opaque-origin preview frame to /compose. The nested Compose page could not fetch /data/catalog.json because its origin was null, so the catalogue stayed unavailable in the small preview.
reproduction: Open /r/cta-product-preview at 1440x900 or 390x844 and wait for the live resource preview.
Activate START COMPOSING inside the preview.
Observe that the main page remains on the resource route, the child frame attempts /compose, and its /data/catalog.json request fails CORS.
console: The preview frame logs a CORS policy error for /data/catalog.json from origin null, followed by a failed-resource message.
The main page also logs the separately tracked Sites inline-bootstrap CSP error (AUD-342).
No uncaught application exception was observed.

network.note: Loaded in the opaque child frame; top-level page URL did not change.

entries.rootCause: The preview uses sandbox="allow-scripts" without top-navigation permission. A normal anchor therefore navigates the child browsing context; Compose then runs with an opaque origin and cannot load the same-origin catalogue.
entries.verification: The pre-fix failure was reproduced in the deployed browser and the initial red local E2E assertion failed because the top-level route stayed on the detail page. The fix sends a bounded typed request only after a trusted anchor click; the trusted parent validates the expected iframe source, opaque origin and resource ID, then displays an explicit user-confirmation link. No sandbox permission or CSP was relaxed. Local Sites Worker E2E passes 6/6 across desktop/mobile for detail-page, Explore-to-detail and direct-preview flows; the full Compose route reaches Catalogue ready and its submit action is enabled. Public v30 remains affected until a saved review version is deployed and rechecked.
entries.limitation: External and internal destinations require a separate confirmation click. This preserves the current opaque preview origin and sandbox boundary.

entries.title: Mobile visual-spectrum preview squeezes its title beside status badges
entries.expected: The illustrative preview header should retain a readable title and status labels on a 390px mobile viewport.
entries.actual: The title and two status badges shared one constrained flex row. The public v30 screenshot shows the title wrapped into three lines; a local browser regression measured a 60px title box against a 40px readability limit.
reproduction: Open / at 390x844 and scroll to Essential → Experimental.
Inspect the illustrative Tessellate Design Preview header before the local CSS fix.
entries.rootCause: A single horizontal flex row placed the title between the T icon and two status badges. The badges reduced the title column enough to force three lines.
entries.verification: A user-visible Sites Worker browser regression failed before the CSS change with a 60px title box, then passed after the mobile header stacks title and badges while retaining the original desktop row. The post-fix mobile screenshot was visually inspected. The test reports no uncaught exceptions, failed requests, or HTTP errors. The visual correction awaits public review verification.

entries.title: Saved Workbench projects cannot open while the full catalogue request is pending or unavailable
entries.expected: A valid browser-local project should open without waiting for catalogue data; catalogue-backed discovery and replacement should load on demand and fail with a recoverable message.
entries.actual: On the deployed v30 code path, Workbench awaited browser-project restoration and /data/catalog.json together before rendering the saved manifest. If the catalogue was slow, the saved project remained behind a loading state; if it failed, Workbench showed a startup error even though the project data was local and valid. The catalogue is not required to render a saved Gold-resource manifest.
reproduction: Seed a valid employee-experience ProjectManifest in browser storage and open /workbench?project=<saved-id>.
Delay /data/catalog.json; the current deployed v30 route does not show the saved project until the catalogue responds.
In the fixed Sites Worker, verify the project opens before any catalogue request; open Library to trigger lazy loading.
Return HTTP 503 for the first Library catalogue request, verify the project stays open and the UI explains the limitation, then retry and verify resources appear.
network: Before: saved-project restoration and the full 324-resource catalogue request were coupled by Promise.all.
After: zero catalogue requests before the saved Workbench renders; one request when Library opens; deliberate first-attempt 503 is shown and retried successfully.
entries.rootCause: WorkbenchShell included full-catalogue fetch and validation in Promise.all with local project restoration, then kept the whole editor behind the shared loading state. Catalogue-backed Library, Resource metadata, replacement, first-run sample generation, and imported showcase/resource routes were not separated from saved-manifest rendering.
entries.verification: The new Sites Worker browser regression failed before the fix in both desktop and mobile profiles, then passed after it. Saved canvas visible time was 2,132ms desktop and 965ms mobile with zero initial catalogue requests; catalogue request occurred only after opening Library. Axe reported zero violations, and there were zero console errors, uncaught exceptions, failed requests, or unexpected HTTP responses. A separate browser regression injected a first-attempt 503, confirmed the saved project remained usable and the error was explained, then retried successfully and displayed Gold resources. Three cold local Chrome DevTools traces with 4x CPU and Fast 4G measured 2,126–2,176ms LCP, 6–11ms TTFB, 2,119–2,170ms render delay, and CLS 0. The static and Sites Worker builds pass. The implementation is committed as ad735b37cdc81966ff1ce5fe6d727e4fd7cba959. The public Site remains v30; deployed closure is pending an approved newer version.
entries.limitation: The test intercepts /data/catalog.json as a slow or failed request; the saved canvas renders because resource implementations are already restricted to the validated Gold runtime. New-project sample generation and imported resource/showcase routes still require catalogue availability, and continue to report startup failure if that required catalogue cannot be loaded.

entries.title: Workbench resource details and replacement skip heading levels
entries.expected: Resource details should follow the Workbench page heading, and resource candidate headings should follow the Replace Resource dialog heading without skipped levels.
entries.actual: A mobile Lighthouse audit and red-to-green Playwright Axe regression reported heading-order violations for the resource inspector h3 and replacement candidate h4. After correction, the rule reports zero violations at 1440x900 and 390x844.
reproduction: Open a saved resource-backed employee-experience project in Workbench.
Select a resource node and open Inspector > Resource.
Open Replace Resource and run Axe heading-order against the visible page.
network: After fix: zero failed requests and zero HTTP errors in desktop and mobile Sites Worker Playwright runs.
entries.rootCause: ResourceTab used h3 directly below the Workbench h1. ReplaceDrawer candidate cards used h4 directly below the dialog h2. The visual classes were correct, but the semantic heading levels skipped their expected parents.
entries.verification: pnpm build passed, building 324 canonical resources, 40 Gold runtime resources, 733 Astro pages, and the Sites Worker artifact. The regression failed before the semantic heading correction and passed after at desktop/mobile. The related dialog-host and visible-label regressions pass in the same test run. Axe heading-order, browser console errors, uncaught exceptions, failed requests, and HTTP errors are zero after the fixes. Public v30 is unchanged; deployed verification is pending.
entries.limitation: Local desktop/mobile verification is complete. The published v30 Site still contains this defect; close only after deployed verification.

entries.title: Replace Resource dialog uses an aside element with dialog role
entries.expected: A modal dialog should use a host element compatible with the dialog role so browser accessibility APIs expose the modal consistently.
entries.actual: Lighthouse Agentic Browsing reported an agent-accessibility-tree failure for aside[role="dialog"]. A focused Playwright regression failed on desktop and mobile before the host element changed; after the fix, both pass. The local Lighthouse snapshot reports Accessibility 100, Agentic Browsing 100, and zero failed audits.
reproduction: Open a saved resource-backed employee project in Workbench.
Select a resource node, open Inspector > Resource, and open Replace Resource.
Inspect the dialog host element and run the Lighthouse snapshot audit.
network: After fix: zero failed requests and zero HTTP errors in desktop/mobile Sites Worker browser checks.
entries.rootCause: The modal was rendered as an aside, whose native complementary semantics conflict with the explicit dialog role in Chrome accessibility APIs.
entries.verification: The new visible-UI regression failed before the host change and passes at 1440x900 and 390x844. It verifies role=dialog, aria-modal=true, and absence of aside[role=dialog]. Local Lighthouse reports 100 Accessibility and Agentic Browsing with zero failed audits. Public v30 remains unchanged; deployed verification is pending.

entries.title: Layer move buttons override their visible labels in the accessible name
entries.expected: The accessible names for the layer actions should include their visible labels so speech-input users can invoke controls by the words they see.
entries.actual: The visible action text is Move up and Move down, but aria-label overrides made the accessible names Move selected layer up and Move selected layer down. Axe label-content-name-mismatch reported both buttons. After removing the overrides, the accessible names match the visible labels and the desktop regression passes.
reproduction: Open a saved project in Workbench at 1440x900.
Select a layer in the Layers panel.
Compare the visible Move up/Move down labels with the accessible button names; run Axe label-content-name-mismatch.
network: After fix: zero failed requests and zero HTTP errors in the Sites Worker browser run.
entries.rootCause: aria-label replaced the text-derived accessible name with a longer phrase that did not contain the visible button label.
entries.verification: The Playwright Axe regression failed before the fix with both move-button selectors. It passes on desktop after removing the overriding aria-label attributes and confirms exact accessible names Move up and Move down. Mobile does not expose these desktop-only layer action controls. Public v30 remains unchanged; deployed verification is pending.

entries.title: Laptop model switch accessible name omits its visible state label
entries.expected: The switch accessible name should preserve its visible Laptop model and Lab text; its On/Off state should remain discoverable to assistive technology.
entries.actual: The switch displayed Laptop model, Lab, and Off/On, but aria-label="Laptop model Lab" overrode the children and omitted the visible state text. Axe reported label-content-name-mismatch. Removing the override derives the name from the displayed children (including Off), and the regression passes on desktop and mobile after opening the mobile Command panel.
reproduction: Open Workbench at desktop or mobile width.
At mobile width, open the Mobile Workbench Command panel.
Inspect the Laptop model switch accessible name against its visible Laptop model, Lab, and Off/On labels; run Axe label-content-name-mismatch.
network: After fix: zero failed requests and zero HTTP errors in desktop/mobile Sites Worker browser runs.
entries.rootCause: An explicit aria-label omitted the visible On/Off state and overrode the complete child text used by the switch.
entries.verification: The desktop regression failed before the fix. It now passes on desktop and mobile (390x844); the mobile test opens the Command navigation and confirms the switch is present. Axe reports no label-content-name-mismatch, and the accessible name includes Lab and Off. Public v30 remains unchanged; deployed verification is pending.
